newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fewer work stoppages in year to Nov 1996 - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Fewer work stoppages in year to Nov 1996 - SNZ.

text.p: Eight work stoppages ended in November 1996 and a total of 75 stoppages ended in the year to November 30, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
The figures compare to nine stoppages in October, and 78 in the year to October.

Of the eight stoppages in November, seven were complete strikes and one was a partial strike. Together they involved 4,922 employees and resulted in the loss of 5,832 person-days of work and about NZ$701,000 in wages and salaries.
Stoppages ending in the November year resulted in the loss of 72,448 person-days of work, 40 percent more than the 51,924 in the November 1995 year.
An estimated $10.3 million in wages and salaries was lost in the year to November, 56 percent more than the $6.6 million in the year to November 1995.
Of the 75 stoppages in the year, 23 were in the manufacturing industry, 13 in education and 10 in health and community services.
There were 39 stoppages in the private sector, and 36 in the public sector. Total losses of work days, wages and salaries were greater in the public sector.
